translations.text: And the Lord called Moses and spoke to him from the tent of testimony, saying:
“Speak to the Israelites and tell them: ‘If someone among you brings gifts to offer to the Lord, you must bring your gifts from the livestock, from your cattle and your sheep.

If he brings his gift as a whole burnt offering from the cattle, he must bring a male without a defect. At the entrance to the tent of testimony, he must bring what he considers choice before the Lord.
And he must lay his hand on the head of the burnt offering that he is going to offer, and appeal to him to have atonement made for him.
And they must slaughter it before the Lord. Aaron’s sons, the priests, must come and pour out its blood beside his altar, which is in front of the tent of testimony.
And Aaron’s sons, who are the priests, must put fire on the altar and arrange wood on the fire.
And Aaron’s sons, the priests, must put the pieces on the head, and the fat on the wood that is on the fire of the altar.
They shall wash its internal organs and its legs with water, and the priest shall offer them all on the altar. It is a burnt offering, a sacrifice with a pleasing aroma to the Lord.
But if he brings his gift to the Lord from his sheep as a whole burnt offering, he must bring a male without a defect, from the lambs or the goats, and lay his hand on its head.
They must slaughter it beside the altar, on the north side, before the Lord. And Aaron’s sons, the priests, must pour its blood all around the altar.
And they must cut it up into pieces. The priests must take the head and the fat and arrange them on the wood that is on the fire on the altar.

And they must wash its internal organs and its legs with water. The priest must take them all and offer them on the altar. It is a whole burnt offering, a sacrifice by fire with a pleasing fragrance to the Lord.
But if you bring a gift of birds as a whole burnt offering to the Lord, he must take his gift from the turtledoves or the pigeons.
And the priest must bring it to the side of the altar and wring off its head. The priest must offer it on the altar, and he must drain its blood onto the base of the altar.
And he must remove its crop and its wings and throw them beside the altar, toward the east, down into the place for the ashes.

And he must tear it open by its wings without dividing it. The priest must offer it on the altar, on the wood that is on the fire. It is a whole burnt offering, a sacrifice by fire with a pleasing fragrance to the Lord.
If someone brings an offering, it shall be fine flour. He shall pour oil over it and put frankincense on it, for it is a sacrifice.

And he must bring it to Aaron’s sons, the priests. The priest must take a handful of the fine flour and oil, together with all the frankincense. The priest must offer the memorial portion on the altar as a sacrifice by fire with a pleasing fragrance to the Lord.
But the rest of the sacrifice will belong to Aaron and his sons. It is a most holy portion of the Lord’s sacrifices.
But if he brings a gift to the Lord, a sacrifice mixed with frankincense, he must bring unleavened loaves made from fine flour mixed with oil, and unleavened wafers spread with oil.
But if the sacrifice comes from a baking pan, it must be fine flour mixed with oil.
And you must break them into pieces and pour oil over them. It is a sacrifice to the Lord.
But if your gift comes from a griddle, they must make it from fine flour with oil.
And he must bring to the Lord his sacrifice, which he will prepare from these things. He must bring it to the priest, and he must bring it up to the altar.
The priest must take the memorial portion from the sacrifice, and the priest must offer it on the altar. It is a sacrifice by fire with a pleasing fragrance to the Lord.
But what remains of the sacrifice will belong to Aaron and his sons. It is a most holy portion of the Lord’s offerings.
You must not prepare with yeast any sacrifice that you bring up to offer to the Lord, for you must not burn any yeast or any honey as an offering by fire to the Lord.’
You shall bring them to the Lord as a gift of firstfruits, but they shall not be offered on the altar as a pleasing aroma by fire to the Lord.
You shall season every gift of your sacrifice with salt. The salt of God's covenant must not be missing from your sacrifices. You shall add salt to every gift you offer.

If you bring the Lord a sacrifice from your first crops, you shall bring your first ears of grain roasted and broken up while still fresh. You shall present the sacrifice of your first ears of grain to the Lord.
Pour oil over it and put frankincense on it, for it is a sacrifice.
The priest shall offer its memorial portion from the broken grain, together with the oil and all its frankincense. It is an offering by fire to the Lord.
If he brings the Lord a gift as a sacrifice of well-being, and brings it from his cattle, whether male or female, he shall bring it before the Lord without any defect.
He shall lay his hands on the head of his offering and slaughter it at the doors of the tent of testimony. Aaron's sons, the priests, shall pour its blood all around the altar of burnt offerings.
From the sacrifice of well-being they shall bring an offering in honor of the Lord: the fat covering the belly and all the other fat spread over it,
the two kidneys and the fat on them that is on the thighs, and the lobe on the liver. He shall remove these along with the kidneys.
Aaron's sons, the priests, shall offer them on the altar, on top of the burnt offerings arranged on the wood over the fire. It is an offering with a pleasing aroma to the Lord.
If his gift is from the sheep, as a sacrifice of well-being to the Lord, whether male or female, he shall bring it without any defect.
If it is a male that he brings as a gift, he shall stand it before the Lord.
He shall lay his hand on the head of his offering and slaughter it at the doors of the tent of testimony. Aaron's sons, the priests, shall pour its blood all around the altar.

From the sacrifice of well-being he shall bring an offering in honor of the Lord: the fat and the tail, without any defect. He shall remove them from there along with the loins, and also the fat stripped from the belly and all the fat of the belly,
together with the two kidneys and the fat on them that is on the thighs, and the lobe on the liver. He shall remove these along with the kidneys,
namely, the priest, and he shall offer them on the altar as fragrant smoke. It is an offering by fire to the Lord.
If his gift is from the goats, he shall stand it before the Lord.
He shall lay his hand on its head and slaughter it before the Lord at the doors of the tent of testimony. Aaron's sons, the priests, shall pour its blood all around the altar.
He shall bring from it his gift as an offering by fire to the Lord: the fat stripped from the belly and all the fat on the belly.
And the two kidneys and all the fat on them, including what is on the thighs, and the lobe of the liver together with the kidneys—he shall remove them from there.
The priest shall offer it on the altar as an offering by fire with a pleasing aroma to the Lord. All fat shall be regarded as belonging to the Lord.
This is a permanent rule throughout your generations, in all the places where you live: you shall not eat any fat or any blood.
The Lord spoke to Moses, saying to him,
"Speak to the Israelites and tell them: If anyone sins unintentionally before the Lord by doing any one of the things that the Lord's commands forbid,

if the anointed priest sins and causes the people to sin, he shall bring a young bull without any defect from the cattle because of the sin he has committed, to offer it by fire to the Lord for his sin.
The priest shall bring it to the door of the tent of testimony before the Lord. He shall lay his hand on the head of the young bull before the Lord and slaughter the young bull before the Lord.
And the priest who has been anointed and purified shall take some of the bull’s blood in his hands and bring it into the tent of testimony.
And the priest shall dip his finger in the blood and sprinkle the blood with his finger seven times before the Lord, toward the holy curtain.

The priest shall put some of the bull’s blood on the horns of the incense altar before the Lord, which is in the tent of testimony. He shall pour all the bull’s blood at the base of the altar of burnt offering, which is at the entrance to the tent of testimony.
And he shall remove all the fat from the bull offered for sin: the fat covering the internal organs and all the fat on the internal organs,
along with the two kidneys and the fat on them, which is on the thighs, and the lobe, or gland, on the liver. He shall remove these along with the kidneys,
just as they are removed from the bull offered as a peace offering. And the priest shall offer them on the altar of burnt offering.
And the bull’s hide, all its flesh, its head, its legs, its entrails, and its dung—
the whole bull shall be taken outside the camp to a clean place, the place where the ashes are poured out. They shall burn it on wood in a fire; they shall burn it where the ashes are poured out.
If the whole congregation of the children of Israel goes astray and a matter is hidden from the congregation’s eyes, or they do any of the things that the Lord’s commandments forbid and commit sin,
and they are informed of the sin they have committed, the congregation shall take a young bull without blemish for its sin, and they shall place it at the entrance of the tent of testimony.
The elders of the congregation shall lay their hands on the bull’s head before the Lord, and they shall slaughter the bull before the Lord.
And the anointed priest shall bring some of the bull’s blood into the tent of testimony.
The priest shall dip his finger in the bull’s blood and sprinkle it seven times before the Lord, in front of the holy curtain.

And the priest shall put some of the blood on the horns of the altar of incense presented before the Lord in the tent of testimony. He shall pour out all the blood at the base of the altar of burnt offerings, which stands at the entrance of the tent of testimony.
He shall remove all its fat from it and offer it on the altar.
He shall do with the bull just as he did with the bull offered for sin; that is how he shall treat it. And the priest shall pray for them, and their sins shall be forgiven.
And they shall take the whole bull outside the camp and burn it just as they burned the first bull, for it is the congregation’s sin offering.
But if a ruler sins and does any of the things that the commandments of the Lord his God forbid, doing it unintentionally,
and he is informed of the sin he has committed, he shall bring his offering: a male goat from the goats, without blemish.
And he shall lay his hand on the goat’s head, and they shall slaughter it in the place where the burnt offerings are slaughtered before the Lord, for it is a sin offering.

And the priest shall take some of the blood of the burnt offering for sin, dip his finger in it, and put it on the horns of the altar of burnt offerings. He shall pour out all its blood at the base of the altar of burnt offerings.
He shall offer all its fat on the altar, just like the fat of the peace offering. And the priest shall plead on his behalf concerning his sin, and it shall be forgiven him.
But if a person from among the people of the land sins unintentionally, doing any of the things that the Lord’s commandments forbid, and commits sin,
When he is informed of the sin he has committed in this matter, he shall bring his offering: a female sheep from the flock, without blemish, for the sin he has committed.
he shall lay his hand on the head of his sin offering, and they shall slaughter the goat offered for sin in the place where the burnt offerings are slaughtered.
And the priest shall take some of the blood with his finger and put it on the horns of the altar of burnt offering. He shall pour out all the blood at the base of the altar.

He shall remove all the fat from it, like the fat there, like the fat that is removed from the peace offering. The priest shall offer it on the altar as a pleasing aroma to the Lord. And the priest shall pray for him, and his sin shall be forgiven.
But if he brings a sheep as an offering for sin, he shall bring a female sheep without blemish.
He must lay his hand on the head of the sheep offered for sin, and it must be slaughtered in the place where the burnt offerings are slaughtered.

The priest must take some of the blood of the sheep offered for sin with his finger and put it on the horns of the altar of burnt offering. He must pour out all the remaining blood at the base of the altar of burnt offering.

He must remove all its fat, just as the fat is removed from the sheep offered as a peace offering. The priest must offer it on the altar of burnt offerings to the Lord. The priest must pray for him concerning the sin he committed, and he will be forgiven.
If a person sins by hearing a call to testify under oath, and he is a witness because he has seen something or knows about it, but does not disclose the matter, he will bear his sin.
Or if a person touches anything unclean, whether a dead animal, or another unclean animal that wild beasts have killed, or unclean creeping creatures when they die,

or if the person touches human uncleanness, or any kind of uncleanness by which someone becomes unclean through touching it, without being aware of it, but afterward becomes aware of it, that person sins.
The lawless person who speaks with his lips about doing evil or good, whatever a person may say under oath, and it is hidden from him, but he then becomes aware of it, sins in one of these things.
He must confess the sin he committed.

He must bring to the Lord, for the sins he committed, a ewe from the sheep or a female goat from the goats as an offering for his sin. The priest must pray concerning his sin, and his sin will be forgiven.
But if he cannot afford a sheep, he must bring two turtledoves or two young pigeons as an offering to the Lord for the sin he committed, one as a sin offering and one as a burnt offering.
He must bring them to the priest. The priest must first take the one to be offered for sin, and the priest must twist its head at its neck without separating it.
He must sprinkle some of the blood of the bird offered for sin on the side of the altar. He must drain the rest of its blood onto the base of the altar, for it is an offering for sin.
He must prepare the second as a whole burnt offering in the prescribed manner. The priest must pray for him concerning the sin he committed, and he will be forgiven.

But if he cannot afford the two turtledoves or the two young pigeons, he must bring as his gift for the sin he committed a tenth of a measure of fine flour as an offering for his sin. He must not pour oil on it or put frankincense on it, because it is an offering for sin.
He must bring it to the priest. The priest must take a handful from it and offer its memorial portion on the altar as a whole burnt offering to the Lord, for it is an offering for sin.
The priest must pray for him concerning the sin he committed in any one of these things, and he will be forgiven. The remainder will belong to the priest, as with the offering of fine flour.
The Lord spoke to Moses, saying to him,

“If a person acts negligently through neglect and sins unintentionally concerning the Lord’s holy things, he must bring before the Lord, for the sin he committed, a ram without blemish from the sheep, valued at twenty silver shekels according to the sanctuary shekel, for the sin he committed.

He must repay what he wrongfully took from the holy things, and he must give the priest the one-fifth share doubled. The priest must pray for him with the ram offered for his sin, and he will be forgiven.
If a person sins by doing any of the things forbidden by the Lord’s commandments, even though he did not know, he sins and will bear his sin.

He must bring to the priest a ram without blemish from the sheep, at a price in copper, as an offering for his sin. The priest must pray for him concerning the ignorance in which he acted without knowing, and he will be forgiven.
For he went astray and acted in ignorance before the Lord.”
And the Lord spoke to Moses, saying:

If a person sins and, through forgetfulness, neglects the Lord’s commandments, and lies to his neighbor about something entrusted to him, or about a partnership, or about something stolen, or wrongs his neighbor in some matter,
or finds something lost and lies about it, and swears falsely about any of these things that people may do and thereby sin,
and if he sins and is found guilty, he shall return what he stole, or what he took by force through wrongdoing, or what was entrusted to him, or the lost thing that was found,
whatever the matter about which he swore falsely. He shall repay the full amount and add one-fifth to it. He shall give it to its owner on the day when he is convicted.
And for his sin he shall bring the Lord a ram without defect from the flock, valued in silver, for what he has done.
The priest shall pray for him before the Lord, and he shall be forgiven for what he has done in any of these things in which he sinned.
And the Lord spoke to Moses, saying to him,

“Command Aaron and his sons, saying to him: This is the law of the burnt offering. This is the offering that shall be placed on the altar all night until morning, and they shall keep the altar’s fire burning so that it does not go out.
The priest shall put on a linen robe and fasten it around his body. He shall remove from the altar the burnt remains of the burnt offering that the fire consumes, and place them beside the altar.
Then he shall take off his robe and put on another robe, and carry the burnt remains outside the camp to a clean place.

They shall keep a fire burning on the altar; it shall not go out. The priest shall burn wood on it in the morning and arrange the burnt offering on it. He shall offer the fat of the peace offering on it.
A fire shall burn continually on the altar and shall not go out.
This is the law of the grain offering that the priests, Aaron’s sons, shall bring and offer before the Lord, in front of the altar.

He shall take from it with his hand some of the grain offering’s fine flour, together with its oil and its frankincense that is on the grain offering. He shall offer its memorial portion on the altar as a burnt offering, a pleasing aroma to the Lord.
Aaron and his sons shall eat what remains of it, unleavened, in a holy place. They shall eat it in the tent of the courtyard of the testimony.
They must not bake it with leaven. I have given it to them as their portion from the Lord’s burnt offerings. It is most holy, like the sin offering and the offering for unintentional wrongdoing.
Every male among the priests shall eat it. This shall be a perpetual ordinance throughout your generations concerning the Lord’s offerings. Anyone who touches them shall be made pure.”
And the Lord spoke to Moses, saying to him,

“This is the gift of Aaron and his sons that they shall offer to the Lord on the day when you anoint him: one-tenth of a measure of fine flour as a continual grain offering. Offer half of it in the morning and the other half in the evening.
They shall prepare these portions with oil in a pan and bake them. He shall bring them crumbled as an offering, a pleasing aroma to the Lord.
The priest from among his sons who is anointed in his place shall prepare it. Everything shall be offered in full to the Lord as a perpetual ordinance.
Every grain offering of a priest shall be burned entirely, and none of it shall be eaten.”
And the Lord spoke to Moses, saying to him,

“Speak to Aaron and his sons, saying to them: This is the law of the sin offering. In the place where the burnt offering is slaughtered, they shall slaughter the sin offering before the Lord. It is most holy.
The priest who offers it shall eat it in a holy place, in the courtyard of the tent of testimony.
Anyone who touches its flesh shall be made pure. If its blood is sprinkled on someone’s garment, they shall wash the garment on which it was sprinkled in a holy place.
The earthenware vessel in which it is cooked shall be broken. But if it is cooked in a bronze vessel, they shall scrub it and rinse it with water.
Every male among the priests may eat these things. They are most holy to the Lord.
Any offerings brought for sin, some of whose blood is taken into the tent of testimony to make atonement in the holy place, shall not be eaten. They shall be burned with fire.
This is the law for the ram that is brought for sin. It is most holy.
In the place where they slaughter the burnt offering, they shall slaughter the ram for unintentional sin before the Lord. He shall pour its blood around the base of the altar.
He shall offer all the [?] upon it, the fat tail and all the fat on the internal organs.
He shall remove from it the pair of kidneys and the fat on them, which is on the sides, and the lobe or membrane on the liver, and its kidneys.
The priest shall offer them up on the altar as an offering to the Lord for sin.
Every male among the priests may eat these things. They are most holy.
The offering for unintentional sin is like the sin offering. The same law applies to them. It shall belong to the priest who makes atonement with it.
The priest who brings a person's offering shall have the skin of the burnt offering that he offers up.
Every offering baked in an oven, and every offering prepared on a hearth or in a pan, shall belong to the priest who offers it up.
Every offering prepared with oil, and those not prepared with oil, shall belong to all the sons of Aaron, with an equal share for each one.
This is the law for the peace offering that is brought to the Lord.
If he brings it as thanksgiving, he shall also bring, along with the thanksgiving offering, loaves of fine flour mixed with oil, unleavened wafers spread with oil, and fine flour mixed with oil.
He shall bring his gift with unleavened loaves, along with his thanksgiving peace offering.
He shall bring a contribution to the Lord from all his offerings and give it to the priest who pours out the blood of the peace offering. It shall belong to that priest.
The meat of the thanksgiving peace offering shall belong to him. They shall eat it on the day he presents it as a gift of honor; they shall not leave any of it until morning.
But if it is a vow, or he gives it voluntarily, they shall eat the gift that he offers up as a sacrifice on the day he brings his sacrifice.
Whatever remains of the meat of the sacrifice until the third day shall be burned with fire.

But if any of its meat is eaten on the third day, the offering shall not be accepted. It shall not be credited to the one who offers it. It is defiled meat for him, and the person who eats any of it shall bear their sin.
If meat touches anything unclean, it shall not be eaten; it shall be burned with fire. Anyone who is clean may eat meat.
But the person who eats any meat from the peace offering belonging to the Lord while their uncleanness is upon them shall be cut off from their people.

The person who touches anything unclean, whether human uncleanness, an unclean animal, or any unclean abomination, and eats meat from the peace offering belonging to the Lord while their uncleanness is upon them shall be cut off from their people.
The Lord spoke to Moses and said to him,
“Speak to the Israelites and tell them: You shall not eat any fat from cattle, sheep, or goats.
The fat of an animal that has died or has been torn by a wild animal may be used for any purpose, but it shall not be eaten.
Anyone who eats fat from the livestock from which you bring a burnt offering to the Lord shall be cut off from their people.
You must not eat any blood from birds or livestock in any of your dwelling places.
Anyone who eats any blood shall be cut off from their people.
And the Lord spoke to Moses, saying to him:
“Speak to the Israelites and tell them: Whoever brings a peace offering to the Lord shall bring his gift to the Lord from the peace offering.
His own hands shall bring the Lord’s burnt offerings: the fat on the breast and the lobe, or gland, on the liver. He shall present them, lifting them up as an offering of honor before the Lord.
And the priest shall offer up the fat on the breast, and the breast shall belong to Aaron and his sons.
And you shall lift off the right thigh and give it to the priest from your sacrifices of well-being.
The one among Aaron’s sons who presents the blood of the sacrifice of well-being and the fat shall have the right thigh as his portion.

For I have taken the breast that is lifted up and the thigh that is set apart from the Israelites, from your sacrifices of well-being, and I have given them to Aaron the priest and his sons as a permanent entitlement from the Israelites.
This is Aaron’s allotted share and his sons’ allotted share from the Lord’s burnt offerings, on the day when you bring them to serve the Lord,
as the Lord commanded these to be given to them by the Israelites on the day when he anointed them, as a permanent regulation throughout your generations.
This is the law concerning burnt offerings, sacrifices for sins, the sacrifice for ignorance, the sacrifice of purification, and the sacrifice of well-being,
as the Lord commanded Moses on Mount Sinai, on the day when he commanded the Israelites to offer up their gifts before the Lord in the wilderness of Sinai.
And the Lord spoke to Moses, saying to him:
“Take Aaron and his sons, his robes, the anointing oil, the calf for the sin offering, the two rams, and the basket of unleavened bread.
And gather the whole congregation at the entrance to the tent of testimony.”
And Moses did as the Lord commanded him. He gathered the whole congregation at the entrance to the tent of testimony.
And Moses spoke to the whole congregation, saying, “This is what the Lord commanded to be done.”
And Moses brought Aaron and his sons and washed them with water.

And he put the tunic on him and fastened the belt around him. He put the robe on him and placed the ephod over his shoulders. He tied it around him with the ephod’s woven band and fastened it securely to him.
And he placed on him the breastpiece of revelation and truth.
And he placed the turban on his head, and on the front of the turban he placed the gold plate that had been consecrated as holy, as the Lord had commanded Moses.
And Moses took some of the anointing oil.

He anointed the tent and everything in it and consecrated it. And he sprinkled some of the oil on the altar seven times. He anointed the altar and consecrated it and all its utensils. He also consecrated the washbasin and its stand.
And Moses poured some of the anointing oil on Aaron’s head, anointed him, and consecrated him.
Moses brought Aaron’s sons forward, dressed them in tunics, tied sashes around them, and put turbans on their heads, as the Lord had commanded Moses.
Moses brought the bull for the sin offering. Aaron and his sons laid their hands on the head of the bull that was to be offered for sin.

They slaughtered it, and Moses took some of the blood and put it with his finger on the horns all around the altar, purifying the altar. He poured the blood onto the base of the altar and consecrated it so that atonement could be made on it.
Moses took all the fat covering the internal organs, the lobe, or gland, on the liver, and the two kidneys with the fat on them, and offered them on the altar.
He burned the bull, its hide, its flesh, and its dung in a fire outside the camp, as the Lord had commanded Moses.
Moses brought the ram for the burnt offering. Aaron and his sons laid their hands on the ram’s head.
Moses slaughtered the ram and poured its blood onto the altar all around.
He cut the ram into pieces, and Moses offered up its parts—the head, the limbs, and the fat.
He washed the entrails and legs with water. Moses offered up the whole ram on the altar as a burnt offering, a sacrifice with a pleasing aroma to the Lord, as the Lord had commanded Moses.
Moses brought the second ram, the ram of ordination. Aaron and his sons laid their hands on the ram’s head.
He slaughtered it, and Moses took some of its blood and put it on the lobe of Aaron’s right ear, on the thumb of his right hand, and on the big toe of his right foot.

Moses brought Aaron’s sons forward. Moses took some of the blood and put it on the lobes of their right ears, on the thumbs of their right hands, and on the big toes of their right feet. Moses poured the blood onto the altar all around.
He took the fat, the tail, the fat covering the belly, the lobe, or gland, of the liver, the two kidneys and the fat on them, and the right thigh.
From the basket of ordination that was before the Lord, he took one loaf of unleavened bread, another loaf soaked in oil, and one flat cake, or wafer. He placed them on the fat and the right thigh.
He placed them all on Aaron’s hands and on his sons’ hands, and lifted them up as an offering before the Lord.
Moses took them from their hands and offered them up on the altar, on the burnt offering of ordination, which was a burnt offering with a pleasing aroma to the Lord.
Moses took the breast from the ram of consecration and lifted it up before the Lord. It became Moses’ portion, as the Lord had commanded Moses.

Moses took some of the anointing oil and some of the blood that was on the altar, and sprinkled them on Aaron and his garments, and on his sons and his sons’ garments. He consecrated Aaron and his garments, and his sons and his sons’ garments along with him.

Moses said to Aaron and his sons, “Cook the meat in the courtyard of the tent of testimony, in the holy place, and eat it there. You are also to eat the bread in the basket of consecration, as the Lord commanded me, saying, ‘Aaron and his sons shall eat it.’
Whatever remains of the meat and the bread, you are to burn in a fire.
You must not go outside the tent of testimony for seven days, until the day when the period of your consecration is completed. For you are to spend seven days consecrating your hands.
As he has done, the Lord commanded on this day that these things be done, so that an offering may be made on your behalf.”

You must remain at the threshold of the entrance to the tent of testimony for seven days, day and night, keeping the Lord’s requirements so that you do not die. For this is what the Lord commanded me.
Aaron and his sons did everything that the Lord had commanded through Moses.
On the eighth day, Moses called Aaron and his sons and the elders of Israel.
Moses said to Aaron, “Take for yourself a bull calf from the herd as a sin offering and a ram as a burnt offering, both without defects, and bring them before the Lord.
You must also speak to the elders of Israel, saying, ‘Take a male goat from the goats as a sin offering, and a bull calf and a lamb, a year old and without defects, as a whole burnt offering,
and a calf and a ram as a peace offering before the Lord, and fine flour mixed with oil, because the Lord will appear among you today.’”
They brought them before the tent of testimony as Moses had commanded them. The whole congregation came and stood before the Lord.
Moses said to them, “This is what the Lord told you to do, and the glory of the Lord will appear among you.”

Moses said to Aaron, “Approach the altar and offer your sacrifice for your sin and your burnt offering, and make atonement for yourself and your household. Bring the people’s offerings and make atonement for them, as the Lord commanded.”
Aaron approached the altar and slaughtered the calf for his sin.
Aaron’s sons brought the blood to him. He dipped his finger in the blood and put it on the horns of the altar, and he poured the blood onto the base of the altar.
He offered on the altar the fat, the kidneys, and the lobe of the gland over the liver of the animal given as a sin offering, as the Lord had commanded through Moses.
He burned the flesh and the hide in a fire outside the camp.
They slaughtered the burnt offering, and Aaron’s sons brought the blood to him. He poured it onto the altar all around.
They brought him the burnt offering piece by piece, together with the head, and they offered them on the altar.
He washed the entrails and the legs with water and offered the burnt offering on the altar.
He presented the people’s offering. He took the male goat for the people’s sin and slaughtered it in the same way as the first one.
He presented the burnt offering and prepared it as required.
He presented the grain offering, filled his hands with some of it, and offered it on the altar, in addition to the morning burnt offering.
He slaughtered the calf and the ram for the people’s peace offering. Aaron’s sons brought the blood to him, and he poured it around the altar.
There was the fat from the calf, the fat tail from the ram, the fat covering the entrails, the two kidneys with the fat on them, and the lobe, or gland, over the liver.
He placed the fat on the breast, and he offered the fat on the altar.
Aaron lifted the breast and the right thigh as a contribution before the Lord, as the Lord had commanded through Moses.
Aaron stretched out his hand over the people. He came down from the altar after he had finished offering the sin offering, the burnt offerings, and the peace offerings.
Moses and Aaron went into the tent of testimony. When they came out, they blessed all the people, and the glory of the Lord appeared to all the people.
And fire came out from the Lord and consumed the burnt offerings and the fat on the altar. All the people saw it and were amazed, and they fell facedown and worshiped.
And Aaron’s two sons, Nadab and Abihu, each took his censer and put incense on them. They brought unauthorized fire before the Lord, which the Lord had not commanded them to bring.
And fire came out from the Lord and consumed them, and they died before the Lord.
Moses said to Aaron, “This is the word that the Lord spoke: ‘Among those who come near me I will show myself holy, and I will give them glory in the whole assembly.’” And Aaron was deeply grieved.
And Moses called Mishael and Elzaphan, the sons of Uzziel, [?] the brother of Aaron’s father, and said to them, “Go and carry your brothers away from the holy place to outside the camp.”
And they went and carried them in their tunics outside the camp, just as the Lord had told Moses.

And Moses said to Aaron and to Eleazar and Ithamar, his surviving sons, “Do not cover your heads or shave them, and do not tear your clothes, so that you do not die and wrath does not come upon the whole assembly. But your brothers, the whole house of Israel, shall weep over the burning that befell them.”
“And you must not go outside the tent of testimony, so that you do not die, for the anointing oil from the Lord is upon you.” And they did as Moses had said.
And the Lord spoke to Aaron, saying:

“You and your sons with you must not drink wine or strong drink when you are about to enter the tent of testimony or approach the altar, so that you do not die. This is a perpetual ordinance throughout your generations.
“And you shall distinguish between what is holy and what is profane, and between what is unclean and what is clean.
“And you shall teach the people of Israel all the ordinances that the Lord declared to them through Moses.”
And Moses said to Aaron and to Eleazar and Ithamar, Aaron’s surviving sons, “Take the offering left over from the Lord’s burnt offerings and eat it unleavened beside the altar. It is most holy.
You shall eat it in the holy place, for this is your prescribed share and the prescribed share of your children, to belong to you from the Lord’s burnt offerings. For this is what I was commanded.”

“And you shall eat the breast set apart and the thigh contributed as an offering in a holy place, you and your sons and your household with you. For it is your allotted portion and your sons’ allotted portion, given to you from the peace offerings of the people of Israel.

“They shall bring the thigh contributed as an offering and the breast laid upon the offerings of fat, to set them apart as a dedicated offering before the Lord. They shall belong to you and to your sons and daughters with you as a perpetual allotted portion, just as the Lord commanded Moses.”
And Moses carefully inquired about the male goat offered for sin, but it had been burned. Moses was angry with Eleazar and Ithamar, Aaron’s surviving sons, and said to them:
“Why did you not eat the goat offered for sin in the holy place? It is most holy. The Lord gave it to you to eat, so that you might thereby bear the assembly’s sin and pray for them before the Lord.
“For none of its blood was brought into the holy place before him. You should have eaten it inside the holy place, just as the Lord commanded me.”

And Aaron spoke to Moses, saying, “Today they brought their sin offerings and their burnt offerings before the Lord, and these things have happened to me. If I ate the sin offerings today, would that please the Lord?”
And Moses heard this, and it pleased him.
And the Lord spoke to Moses and Aaron, saying to them:
“Speak to the people of Israel and tell them, ‘These are the animals you may eat from among all the animals on the earth.’”
Any animal among the livestock that has a divided hoof, with the hoof split into parts, and chews the cud—these are the animals you may eat.
But among these, among those that chew the cud and those that have divided, split hooves, you must not eat the camel, because it chews the cud but its hoof is not divided. It is unclean for you.
And the hare, the rabbit, because it chews the cud but its hoof is not divided. It is unclean for you.
And the rock badger, because it brings up and chews the cud but its hoof is not divided. It is unclean for you.
And the pig, because its hoof is divided and split into parts, but it does not chew the cud. It too is unclean for you.
You must not eat their flesh, and you must not touch their dead bodies. These are unclean for you.
And these are what you may eat among all the creatures in the waters: anything that has fins and scales in the waters, in the seas and in the streams—these you may eat.

And anything that has neither fins nor scales in the waters, whether in the seas or in the streams, among all the creatures that the waters bring forth and among every living creature in the waters, is detestable.
And they shall be detestable to you. You must not eat their flesh, and you must reject their dead bodies.
And anything among the creatures in the waters that has neither fins nor scales is detestable to you.
And these are the birds you must reject and not eat; instead, they shall be detestable: the eagle, the vulture and the sea eagle,
and the vulture and the kite, and those resembling them,
and the raven and those resembling it,
And the ostrich, the owl, the gull and those like them, and the hawk and those like it.
and the night raven and the cormorant and the owl,
and the swan and the pelican, that is, the pelican, and the purple swamphen,
and the heron, that is, the heron, and the plover and those resembling it, and the hoopoe and the bat, that is, the bat.
And all flying creatures resembling birds that walk on four feet shall be detestable to you.
But these you may eat among the creatures resembling birds that walk on four feet: those that have joints above their feet with which they leap on the ground.

And these are what you may eat among them: the wingless locust and those resembling it, and the locust and those resembling it, and the grasshopper and those resembling it, and the snake-fighting locust and those resembling it.
Anything shaped like a bird that has four feet shall be detestable to you.
And by these you will become unclean: anyone who touches their dead bodies will be unclean until evening.
And anyone who carries any of their dead bodies must wash their clothes and will be unclean until evening.

And among all the livestock, anything that has a divided hoof, with the hoof split into parts, but does not chew the cud shall be unclean for you. Anyone who touches their dead bodies will be unclean until evening.
And anything that walks on its paws among all the wild animals that walk on four feet shall be unclean for you. Anyone who touches their dead bodies will be unclean until evening.
And anyone who carries their dead bodies must wash their clothes and will be unclean until evening. These shall be unclean for you.
These will be unclean for you among the crawling creatures that move on the earth: the weasel, the mouse, and the land crocodile.
And the shrew, or shrew mouse, the chameleon, the gecko, the lizard, and the mole.
These will be unclean for you among all the creatures that move on the earth. Anyone who touches their dead bodies will be unclean until evening.

Anything on which one of their dead bodies falls will be unclean, whether a wooden utensil, a garment, a skin, or sackcloth. Any utensil used for work must be washed in water. It will be unclean until evening, and then it will be clean.
Every clay vessel on which one of these falls inside the house will be unclean, and they must be broken.
Any food that is eaten will be unclean if things of this kind come onto it. Anything that is drunk from any vessel will be unclean.
Anything on which one of these dead creatures falls will be unclean. Ovens and hearths must be torn down, because they are unclean, and they will be unclean for you.
But a spring of water, a well, and a collection of water will remain clean. Anyone who touches their dead bodies, however, will be unclean.
If one of their dead bodies falls on any seed that is to be sown, it will remain clean.
But if water is poured onto any seed and one of their dead bodies falls on it, it will be unclean for you.
If one of the animals that you may eat dies, anyone who touches its dead body will be unclean until evening.

Anyone who eats from their dead bodies must wash his clothes and will be unclean until evening. Anyone who carries their dead bodies must wash his clothes and bathe in water, and he will remain unclean until evening.
Every crawling creature that moves on the earth will be detestable to you, and you must not eat it.
Anything that moves on its belly, and anything that always walks on four feet, among all the crawling creatures that move on the earth—you must not eat it, because it is detestable to you.
You must not make yourselves detestable through any of the crawling creatures that move on the earth. You must not defile yourselves with these or become unclean through them.
For I am the Lord your God. You must purify yourselves and be holy, because I, your God, am holy. You must not defile yourselves through any of the crawling creatures that move on the earth.
For I am the Lord who brought you out of the land of Egypt to be your God. You must be holy, because I, the Lord, am holy.
This is the law concerning animals, crawling creatures, birds, every living creature that moves in the waters, and every living creature that moves on the earth,
to distinguish between what is unclean and what is not unclean, and between the living creatures that may be eaten and the living creatures that may not be eaten.
The Lord spoke to Moses, saying to him,

“Speak to the people of Israel and tell them: If a woman conceives and gives birth to a male child, she will be unclean for seven days. According to the rule for her menstruation, she will be unclean for seven days.
On the eighth day she must circumcise the flesh of his foreskin.
She must spend thirty-three days remaining in the blood of her impurity. She must not touch anything holy or enter the sanctuary until the days of her purification are completed.
But if she gives birth to a female child, she will be unclean for fourteen days according to the rule for her menstruation. She must spend sixty-six days in the blood of her defilement.

When the days of her purification for a son or a daughter are completed, she must bring a year-old lamb without blemish to be offered as a whole burnt offering, and a young pigeon or a turtledove as a sin offering, to the entrance of the tent of testimony, to the priest.
He shall bring it before the Lord, and the priest shall pray over it and cleanse her from the flow of her blood. This is the law for a woman who gives birth to a boy or a girl.

But if she cannot afford the required lamb, she shall take two turtledoves or two young pigeons, one turtledove for a burnt offering and the other for a sin offering. The priest shall pray on her behalf, and she shall become clean.
And the Lord spoke to Moses and Aaron, saying to them:

If a person develops a scar or a white spot on the skin of his body, and it becomes a lesion of leprosy on the skin of his body, he shall be brought to Aaron the priest or to one of his sons who serves as a priest.

The priest shall examine the lesion on the skin of his body. If the hair has changed and become white, and the mark of the lesion is sunken into the skin of his body, it is a lesion of leprosy. The priest shall examine him and declare him unclean.

But if the spot is very white on the skin of his body, and his lesion is sunken or faint in his skin, and his hair has not changed into white hair, but the spot is dark or [?], the priest shall isolate his lesion for seven days.

The priest shall inspect the lesion on the seventh day. If he sees that the lesion remains unchanged and has not changed on the skin of his body, the priest shall isolate him again for another seven days.

The priest shall examine him on the seventh day for the second time. If the sore is darkened or faded, and the sore has not changed in the skin of his body, the priest shall declare him clean, for what is on him is a spot. He shall wash his clothes and be clean.
But if the spot changes on the skin of his body after the priest has examined him and declared him clean, he shall come before the priest a second time.
The priest shall inspect him. If the spot has changed on the skin of his body, the priest shall declare him unclean. It is leprosy.
If a person develops a lesion of leprosy, he shall come before the priest.
The priest shall examine him. If a white scar has developed on the skin of his body and has made the hair turn white, with [?] healthy flesh within the scar,
it is persistent leprosy on the skin of his body. The priest shall declare him unclean and isolate him, because he is unclean.
But if the leprosy breaks out over the skin of his body and covers all the skin of his body, from his head to his feet, wherever the priest can see,
the priest shall examine him. If the leprosy has covered all the skin of his body, the priest shall declare the person with leprosy clean, because he has turned entirely white. He is clean.
But on the day that living flesh appears on him, he shall become unclean.
The priest shall examine the healthy flesh and declare him unclean because of the healthy flesh. For he is unclean, because it is leprosy.
But if the healthy flesh heals and the white area changes, he shall come before the priest.
The priest shall examine him, and if the sore has turned white, the priest shall declare the sore clean, and he shall be clean.
If an ulcer develops in the flesh on the skin of his body and heals,
and a scar develops where the sore was, white or reddish with a whitish appearance or fiery red, he shall present it before the priest.

The priest shall examine him. If its lesion is sunken below the skin of his body and his hair has changed and become white, the priest shall declare him unclean, because it is leprosy that has developed in the ulcer and broken out on him.

But if the priest inspects it and finds that no white hair has developed in it and no sunken lesion has developed in the skin of his body, and the scar is dark, the priest shall isolate him for seven days.
But if it changes on the skin of his body, the priest shall declare him unclean. It is a lesion of leprosy that has broken out in his sore.
But if the spot remains on his body and does not spread, it is a scar from his ulcer. The priest shall declare him clean.
If the flesh on the skin of his body is burned by fire, and the healed place of the burn becomes a white, fiery-red spot on his skin, or changes color and becomes white,

The priest shall examine him, and if the hair at the affected spot has turned white and the lesion is deeper than his skin, it is leprosy that has broken out in the boil. The priest shall declare him unclean; it is a leprous lesion.
But if the priest examines him and there is no white hair in the affected spot, and the spot is not deeper than the skin of his body but is faded, the priest shall isolate him for seven days.
The priest shall examine him on the seventh day. If it has spread across the skin of his body, the priest shall declare him unclean. It is leprosy that has broken out in his burn.
But if the white patch stays in its place and does not spread in his skin, and remains faded, it is the scar of the boil. The priest shall declare him clean, for it is the mark of his boil.
And if a man or woman develops a leprous lesion on the head or beard,

The priest shall look at the sore. If it appears deeper than the skin of his body and there is thin yellowish hair in it, the priest shall declare him unclean, for it is a scaly sore: leprosy of his head or leprosy of his beard.

and the priest examines the lesion of his scaly infection and finds that it does not appear deeper than the skin of his body, and there is no reddish hair in it, the priest shall isolate the lesion of his scaly infection for seven days.

The priest shall examine its appearance on the seventh day, and if his scaly infection has not spread, there is no reddish hair in it, and the lesion of his scaly infection is not deeper than the skin of his body,
he shall shave himself, but you shall not shave his scaly infection. The priest shall isolate him for seven days a second time.

The priest shall examine his scaly infection on the seventh day, and if his scaly infection has not spread in the skin of his body after he has shaved himself, and his scaly infection does not appear deeper than the skin of his body, the priest shall declare him clean. He shall wash his clothes and be clean.
But if his scaly infection spreads in the skin of his body after he has been cleansed,
the priest shall examine him, and if the scaly infection has spread in the skin of his body, the priest shall not look for reddish hair, because he has become unclean.
But if the scaly infection on his body remains unchanged in his sight, and black hair grows in it, the scaly infection has healed. The person shall be clean, and the priest shall declare him clean.
If a man or a woman has a white, shining patch on the skin of the body,
The priest shall examine him, and if the white patches are in the skin of his flesh, he is clean.
But if his hair recedes from his forehead, he is bald; he is clean.
but the hair of his head has fallen out at the front, this is frontal baldness—that is, a bald forehead. He is clean.
But if a white or reddish spot, or a leprous reddish spot, develops on his bald crown or bald forehead,
the priest shall examine him, and if the spot of his lesion is white or reddish on his bald crown or bald forehead, resembling leprosy in the skin of his body,
he is a leprous person and is unclean. The priest shall declare him unclean; the sign of his leprosy is on his head.
The leprous person who has leprosy shall wear torn clothes, and his head shall be uncovered. He shall cover the area around his mouth, and they shall call him unclean.
Unclean. Throughout all the days that he spends with the leprous lesion on him, he shall be unclean. He shall live apart, and his dwelling shall be outside the camp.
If a garment has a leprous sore in it, whether a garment of plant fiber, or a garment of linen or wool,
or in the warp or the weft, or in linen or wool, or in a hide or any hide used for making things,
And if the lesion is greenish or reddish in the garment, leather, warp, weft, or any leather article used for work, this lesion is leprosy. He shall show these things to the priest.
The priest shall examine the lesion, and the priest shall isolate that lesion for seven days.

The priest shall examine the lesion on the seventh day. If that lesion has spread in the garment, warp, weft, or leather, whatever kind of work is done with the leather, the lesion is persistent leprosy; it is unclean.
He shall burn the garment, warp, weft, wool, linen, or any leather articles if the lesion of persistent leprosy is in them. They shall burn them in a fire.
But if the priest examines it and that lesion has not continued to spread in the garment, warp, weft, or any leather article,
The priest shall give orders to wash the item that has the infection on it, and the priest shall isolate that infection for another seven days.

The priest shall examine it after the infection has been washed. If the infection has not changed its appearance, even though it has not spread, it is unclean. It shall be burned in fire, because it has become established in the garment, the warp, or the weft.
If the priest sees that the infection has faded after it has been washed, he shall tear it out of the garment, the leather, the warp, or the weft.
But if it appears again in the garment, the warp, the weft, or any leather article, it is leprosy that has broken out. They shall burn in fire whatever has that infection in it.
The garment, the warp, the weft, or any leather article that has been washed and from which that infection has disappeared shall be washed again, and it shall be clean.
This is the law concerning an infection of leprosy in a woolen garment, linen garments, warp, weft, or any leather article, for declaring it clean or unclean.
And the Lord spoke to Moses, saying:
For this is the law concerning someone with leprosy on the day of his cleansing: he shall be brought before the priest.
The priest shall go outside the camp, and the priest shall examine him. If the infection of leprosy has disappeared from the person with leprosy,
the priest shall give orders to obtain for the person being cleansed two living, clean birds, cedarwood, spun scarlet yarn, and hyssop.
The priest shall give orders to slaughter one of the birds in an earthenware vessel over fresh running water.

He shall take the other, living bird, along with the cedarwood, the scarlet yarn, and the hyssop, and dip them, together with the living bird, in the blood of the bird slaughtered over fresh running water.
He shall sprinkle the person being cleansed of his leprosy seven times, and he shall be clean. He shall release the living bird into the open field.

The person being cleansed shall wash his clothes, shave off all his hair, and bathe in water, and he shall be clean. After this, he shall enter the camp, but he shall remain outside his house for seven days.

On the seventh day he shall shave off all his hair: the hair on his head, his beard, and his eyebrows. He shall shave off every hair on him, wash his clothes, and bathe his body in water, and he shall be clean.

On the eighth day he shall take two lambs without blemish, each a year old, and one sheep without blemish, a year old, along with three tenths of a measure of fine flour mixed with oil as an offering, and one log of oil.
The priest who performs the cleansing shall present the person being cleansed, together with these other things, before the Lord at the entrance to the tent of testimony.
The priest shall take one of the lambs and present it as an offering for sin, together with the log of oil, and set them apart as an offering before the Lord.

They shall slaughter the lamb in the place where they slaughter the offerings for sin and the animal to be made a burnt offering; they shall do this in the holy place. For the animal slaughtered for sin, like the one offered for an unintentional offense, belongs to the priest. It is most holy.

The priest shall take some of the blood of the animal offered for sin, and the priest shall put it on the tip of the right ear of the person being cleansed, on the thumb of his right hand, and on the big toe of his right foot.
The priest shall take some oil from the log and pour it onto the priest’s left hand.
The priest shall dip his right finger into the oil on his left hand, and with his finger he shall sprinkle it seven times before the Lord.

The priest shall put some of the oil remaining in his hand on the tip of the right ear of the person being cleansed, on the thumb of his right hand, and on the big toe of his right foot, over the blood of the animal offered for sin.
The priest shall put the oil remaining on his hand on the head of the person being cleansed, and the priest shall pray for him before the Lord.
The priest shall prepare the sin offering and pray for the person being cleansed from his sin. After this, the priest shall slaughter the burnt offering.
The priest shall offer up the burnt offering and the grain offering on the altar before the Lord. The priest shall pray for him, and he shall be clean.

But if he is poor and cannot afford what he must give, he shall take one lamb as an offering for the sin he has committed, to be lifted up so that prayer may be made for him, and one-tenth of a measure of fine flour mixed with oil as a grain offering, and one log of oil.
He shall also take two turtledoves or two young pigeons, whichever he can afford. One turtledove shall be given as a sin offering, and the other as a burnt offering.
On the eighth day he shall bring them for his cleansing to the priest at the entrance of the tent of testimony, before the Lord.
The priest shall take the lamb to be given as a sin offering and the log of oil, and the priest shall lift them up as an offering before the Lord.

He shall slaughter the lamb as a sin offering. The priest shall take some of the blood of the lamb offered for sin and put it on the right earlobe of the person being cleansed, on the thumb of his right hand, and on the big toe of his right foot.
The priest shall pour some of the oil onto his left hand.
Then the priest shall use his right finger to sprinkle some of the oil in his left hand seven times before the Lord.

The priest shall put some of the oil in his hand on the right earlobe of the person being cleansed, on the thumb of his right hand, and on the big toe of his right foot, on the places where the blood of the sin offering was put.
He shall put the oil remaining in the priest’s hand on the head of the person he has cleansed, and the priest shall pray for him before the Lord.
He shall bring one of the turtledoves or young pigeons, according to what he can afford.
One of them shall be a sin offering, and the other a burnt offering, together with the grain offering. The priest shall pray for the person being cleansed before the Lord.
This is the law for someone who has a leprous lesion and cannot afford the offerings for his cleansing.
The Lord said to Moses and Aaron:
“I will put, or reveal, leprous lesions in the houses in that land.
The owner of the house shall come and inform the priest, saying, ‘What I have seen in my house may be a leprous lesion.’
The priest shall order the furnishings of the house to be removed before the priest goes inside to inspect the house, so that the things in the house do not become unclean. After this,
the priest shall inspect the leprous lesion on the walls of the house: greenish or reddish hollows that appear sunken into the walls of the house.
The priest shall go outside the house to its entrance, and the priest shall isolate the house for seven days.
The priest shall return on the seventh day to inspect the house, and behold, the leprous lesion has spread on the walls of the house.
the priest shall order them to remove the stones on which the leprous sore has appeared. They shall throw them outside the city into an unclean place.
They shall scrape the inside of the house all around and pour out the earth they have scraped off outside the city into an unclean place.
They shall take other stones that have been hewn and put them in place of the stones removed from there. They shall also take fresh earth and plaster the house.
But if the leprous lesion returns and breaks out in the house after the stones have been removed, after the house has been scraped, and after it has been plastered again,
the priest shall go inside and examine whether the leprous lesion has spread in the house. It is persistent leprosy in the house; that house is unclean.
They shall demolish it, and they shall take its wood, its stones, and all its earth outside the city to an unclean place.
And anyone who enters the house during any of the days it remains shut up shall be unclean until evening.
And anyone who sleeps in the house shall wash his clothes and be unclean until evening. And anyone who eats in the house shall wash his clothes and be unclean until evening.

But if the priest comes and enters and looks, and the leprous sore has not spread in the house after the house was plastered, the priest shall declare the house clean, because that mark has disappeared from it.
