And anyone who sits on an object [?] on which the man with a discharge sits shall wash his clothes and bathe in water.
[?] And he shall bathe his body in water and be unclean until evening.
And an earthenware vessel [?] that the man with a discharge touches shall be broken. And every wooden vessel shall be rinsed in water and become clean.
But when the man with a discharge becomes clean from the discharge of his body, he shall count seven days for his purification. He shall wash his clothes and bathe his body in water [?].
[?] in it shall be rinsed in water, and he shall be unclean until evening.
And a woman [?] a man sleeps [?] emitting semen [?]. They shall bathe in water and be unclean until evening.
And a woman whose blood flows from her, whose discharge is in her body, shall remain in her separation for seven days [?]. Everyone [?] shall be unclean.
[?] seven days [?] sleeping [?] on it shall be unclean.
And a woman, if her flow of blood continues for many days [?] the time of her menstruation [?] until [?] her discharge, her impurity [?], shall be unclean.

And every bed on which she sleeps during all the days of her discharge shall be for her like the bed of her menstruation. And every object on which she sits shall be unclean, like the impurity of her menstruation.
Everyone who touches them shall be unclean. He shall wash his clothes and wash his body in water, and be unclean until evening.
But if she becomes clean from her discharge, she shall count seven days for herself, and after these she shall be clean.
On the eighth day she shall take two turtledoves or two young pigeons and bring them before the priest at the entrance to the tent of testimony.
And the priest shall offer one of them as a sin offering and the other as a burnt offering. The priest shall make atonement for her before the Lord for the discharge of her impurity.
And you shall make the children of [?] fear their impurities, so that they do not die because of their impurities by defiling my tabernacle that is among them.
This is the law for the man with a discharge, and for anyone from whom semen comes out, defiling a bed so that he becomes unclean in it,
and for the woman whose blood flows from her during her menstruation, and for anyone with a discharge, whether a man or a woman, and for the man who sleeps with someone who is menstruating.
And the Lord spoke to Moses after Aaron's two sons died, when they offered unauthorized fire before the Lord and died.

And the Lord spoke to Moses, saying to him, "Speak to Aaron your brother, so that he does not enter the holy place at any time, inside the curtain, before the atonement cover that is on the ark of the testimony, so that he does not die. For I will appear in the cloud over the atonement cover."
And this is how Aaron shall enter the holy place: with a calf from the herd as a sin offering and a ram as a burnt offering.

And he shall put on a holy linen tunic, and linen undergarments shall be on his body. He shall fasten a linen sash around himself and put on a cloth turban, for these are holy clothes. He shall wash his whole body in water and put them on.
And he shall take from the congregation of the children of Israel two male goats from the goats as a sin offering and one ram as a burnt offering.
Aaron shall bring his bull as a sin offering and make atonement for himself and his household.
And he shall take the two goats and present them before the Lord at the entrance to the tent of testimony.
Aaron shall cast lots over the two goats: one lot for the Lord and one lot for what is called the scapegoat, that is, the one to be sent away.
And Aaron shall bring the goat on which the Lord’s lot fell and offer it as a sin offering.

And the other goat, on which the lot fell for the scapegoat, that is, the one to be sent away, he shall present alive before the Lord to make atonement over it, so that he may send it away to the place of release and leave it in the wilderness.
And Aaron shall bring his bull as a sin offering and make atonement for himself and his household. He shall slaughter his bull as an offering for his sin.
And he shall take the censer full of burning coals from the altar before the Lord, and he shall fill his hands with incense from the selected mixture and bring it inside the curtain.
And he shall put the incense on the fire before the Lord, and the smoke of the incense shall cover the atonement cover that is over the testimony, so that he does not die.

And he shall take some of the bull’s blood and sprinkle it with his finger on the east side of the atonement cover. He shall sprinkle some of the blood with his finger seven times in front of the atonement cover.

And he shall slaughter the bull for the sins of the people before the Lord, and bring some of its blood inside the curtain. He shall do with its blood as he did with the bull’s blood, and sprinkle its blood on the atonement cover and in front of the atonement cover.

And he shall make atonement for the holy places because of the impurities of the children of Israel and because of their transgressions, for all their sins. This is how you shall deal with the tent of testimony, which they erected among them in the midst of their impurity.

And no one shall approach the tent of testimony when he goes in to make atonement in the holy place, until he comes out. And he shall make atonement for himself, his household, and the entire assembly of the children of Israel.
And he shall come out to the altar before the Lord and make atonement for it. He shall take some of the bull’s blood and some of the male goat’s blood and put it on the horns of the altar all around.
And he shall sprinkle some of the blood on it with his finger seven times, cleanse it, and purify it from the impurities of the children of Israel.
And he shall finish making atonement in the holy place, the tent of testimony, and the altar. And he shall [?] for the priests, and he shall bring the living goat.

Aaron shall place both his hands on the head of the living goat and declare over it all the lawless deeds of the children of Israel, all their transgressions, and all their sins. He shall put them on the head of the living goat and send it away into the wilderness by the hand of a man who is ready.
The goat shall carry all their wrongdoing upon itself to a land where no one travels, and he shall send the goat away into the wilderness.
Aaron shall enter the tent of testimony and take off the linen garment that he put on when entering the holy place, and he shall leave it there.

He shall wash his body with water in a holy place and put on his garment. He shall come out and offer his burnt offering and the people’s burnt offering, and make atonement for himself, his household, and the people, as for the priests.
And he shall place the fat of the sin offering on the altar.
And he shall send away the goat that was set apart for release. He shall wash his clothes and bathe his body in water, and after this he shall enter the camp.

And the bull for the sin offering and the other goat for the sin offering, whose blood was brought into the holy place to make atonement there, he shall take outside the camp. They shall burn their hides, their flesh, and their dung in a fire.
But the one who burns them shall wash his clothes and bathe his body in water, and after this he shall enter the camp.
This shall be a permanent statute for you: in the seventh month, on the tenth day of the month, you shall humble yourselves and do no work, both the native-born and the foreigner living among you.
For on this day he shall make atonement for you to cleanse you from all your sins, so that you may be pure before the Lord.
You shall have sabbaths of complete rest, and you shall humble yourselves. This is a permanent statute.
The priest who is anointed and ordained to serve in his father's place shall make atonement for you. He shall put on the linen robe, a holy robe.
He shall make atonement for the Holy of Holies. He shall also make atonement for the tent of testimony and the altar, and he shall make atonement for the other priests and the whole congregation.
This shall be a permanent statute for you: to make atonement for all the children of Israel for all their sins once a year. They shall do this as the Lord commanded Moses.
And the Lord spoke to Moses, saying to him:
Speak to Aaron, his sons, and all the children of Israel, and tell them: This is what the Lord has commanded, saying:
Any person among the children of Israel or among the foreigners who slaughters a calf, a sheep, or a goat in the camp, and anyone who slaughters in the camp,

and does not bring them outside the tent of testimony to offer it as a whole burnt offering for well-being, acceptable as a pleasing fragrance—and anyone who slaughters outside and does not bring them to the entrance of the tent of testimony to offer the gift to the Lord before the tent of testimony—this shall be counted as bloodshed against that person. He has shed blood. That person shall be cut off from his people.

So that the Israelites may bring the sacrifices they intend to slaughter in the fields, and bring them before the Lord, to the entrance of the tent of testimony, to the priest, and slaughter them as peace offerings to the Lord.
The priest shall pour its blood onto the altar before the Lord, at the entrance of the tent of testimony, and shall offer up the fat as a pleasing fragrance before the Lord.

They shall no longer turn to slaughter their sacrifices to worthless things, with which they prostitute themselves by following them. This shall be a permanent statute for you throughout your generations.
And you shall tell them: Any person among the children of Israel or among the children of the foreigners who have joined you, who brings a whole burnt offering or a sacrifice,
and does not bring it to the entrance of the tent of testimony to offer it up, shall be cut off from his people.

And if any person among the children of Israel or among the children of the foreigners who have joined you eats any blood, I will set my face against the person who eats the blood and destroy him from among his people.
For the life of all flesh is its blood, and I have given it to you on the altar to make atonement for your lives. For it is its blood with which he will make atonement in place of a life.
Therefore I told the children of Israel: No person among you shall eat blood, and neither the foreigners nor the person who has joined you shall eat blood.

And any person among the children of Israel or among the foreigners who have joined you, who hunts and catches a wild animal or a bird that may be eaten, shall pour out its blood and draw earth over it to cover it.
For the life of all flesh is its blood. And I told the children of Israel: You shall not eat any blood of any flesh, because the life of all flesh is its blood. Anyone who eats it shall be cut off.

And any person, whether a native or a foreigner, who eats a dead animal or one attacked by a wild animal shall wash his clothes and bathe in water. He shall remain unclean until evening, and then he shall be clean.
If he does not wash his clothes and does not bathe his body in water, he shall bear his guilt.
And the Lord spoke to Moses, saying to him:
Speak to the children of Israel and tell them: I am the Lord your God.

You shall not act according to the practices of the land of Egypt, where you lived, nor shall you act according to the practices of the land of Canaan, into which I am bringing you. You shall not follow their customs.
You shall carry out my judgments and keep my commands, following them, for I am the Lord your God.
You shall keep all my commands and all my judgments and carry them out. A person who carries them out will live by them. I am the Lord your God.
No one must approach a member of his own family, a blood relative, to uncover her nakedness. I am the Lord.
You must not uncover your father's nakedness or your mother's nakedness. She is your mother; you must not uncover her nakedness.
You must not uncover the nakedness of your father's wife.
You must not uncover the nakedness of your sister, your father’s daughter or your mother’s daughter, whether [?] born at home or born outside.
You must not uncover the nakedness of your son's daughter or your daughter's daughter, because it is your own nakedness.
You must not uncover the nakedness of the daughter of your father's wife. She is your sister through your father; you must not uncover her nakedness.
You must not uncover the nakedness of your father's sister, for your father's sister is righteous.
You must not uncover the nakedness of your mother's sister, for your mother's sister is righteous.
You must not uncover the nakedness of your father's brother, and you must not go in to his wife, for he is your relative.
You must not uncover your daughter-in-law's nakedness. She is your son's wife; you must not uncover her nakedness.
You must not uncover the nakedness of your brother's wife, because it is your brother's nakedness.

You must not uncover the nakedness of your son's wife and her daughter. You must not take her son's daughter or her daughter's daughter to uncover their nakedness, for they are your companions or your people, and it is a shameful act.
You must not take a woman in addition to her sister as a rival, to uncover your nakedness with her while her sister is still alive.
You must not approach a woman who is set apart in her uncleanness to uncover her nakedness.
You must not approach your neighbor's wife to sleep with her and defile her.
You must not give any of your offspring to serve a ruler, and you must not defile the holy name, for I am the Lord.
You must not sleep with a male as you would sleep with a woman, for it is an abomination.
You must not approach any animal to sleep with it, give it your semen, and defile yourself with it. A woman must not give herself to any animal to defile herself with it, for it is a disgrace.
Do not defile yourselves with any of these things, for the nations that I am going to drive out before you defiled themselves with all these things.
The land became defiled because of them. I repaid them for their wrongdoing because of it, and the land vomited out those who lived on it.
You must keep all my statutes and all my commands and not practice [?] any of these abominations, neither the native nor the foreigner who has joined you.
For the people of the land who lived there before you committed all these detestable acts, and the land became defiled.
Then the land will not vomit you out too when you defile it, as it vomited out the nations that were there before you.
For anyone who practices any of these abominations—the people who do these things will be cut off from among their people.
You must keep my [?], so that you do not practice the things I detested that existed before you, and do not defile yourselves with them, for I am the Lord your God.
And the Lord spoke to Moses, saying:
Speak to the assembly of the people of Israel and tell them: Be holy, because I, the Lord your God, am holy.
Each person must reverence his father and his mother, and you must keep my Sabbaths, for I am the Lord your God.
And when you slaughter a sacrifice of well-being to the Lord, you must offer it so that it is acceptable.
You must eat it on the day you slaughter it and on the following day. If anything remains on the third day, you must burn it in a fire.
But if it is eaten on the third day, it is not a sacrifice; it will not be accepted.
Whoever eats it will bear his sin, because he has defiled the Lord’s holy things. Those who eat these things will be cut off from their people.
And when you reap the harvest of your land, you must not reap your field completely. You must not gather up what falls to the ground from your harvest.

You must not go over your vineyard again to harvest it, nor gather the grapes that fall to the ground in your vineyard. You must leave them for the poor and the foreigners living among you, for I am the Lord your God.
You must not steal, deceive, or lie to one another.
You must not swear by my name for an unjust purpose, nor defile the name of your God. I am the Lord your God.
You must not wrong your neighbor or rob him, and the wages of a hired worker must not remain in your hands
until morning. You must not speak a false word against a deaf person, nor place a stumbling block before a blind person. You must fear the Lord your God, for I am the Lord your God.
You must not act unjustly in judgment. You must not favor the poor or admire [?] a powerful person. You must judge your neighbor fairly.
You must not go about deceitfully among your people. You must not gather deceitfully to threaten your neighbor’s life, for I am the Lord your God.
You must not hate your brother in your heart. You must firmly rebuke your neighbor, so that you do not bring sin upon yourself because of him.
You must not take revenge with your own hand or be angry with the members of your people. You must love your neighbor as yourself. I am the Lord.
You must keep my law. You must not mate your livestock with another kind. You must not sow your vineyard with two kinds of seed. A garment woven in two colors is not good; you must not wear it.

If someone has sexual intercourse with a woman who is a slave reserved to be given to a man, and she has not been redeemed, [?] freedom has not been given to her, their case must be investigated. They must not be put to death, because she has not been freed.
He must bring a ram as a sin offering for his sin to the entrance of the tent of testimony.
The priest must pray over him with the ram of the sin offering before the Lord, for the sin he has committed.

When you enter the land that the Lord your God will give you and plant any tree for food, you must cleanse its fruit of its impurity. For three years it will remain unpurified for you; you must not eat it.
In the fourth year, all its fruit will be holy, blessed to the Lord.
In the fifth year, you may eat its fruit, and its produce will increase for you. I am the Lord your God.
You must not eat on the altars, practice divination, or pay attention to the behavior of birds to read omens from them.
You must not leave locks of hair on yourselves from the hair of your head, nor damage or shave your beards.
You must not wear a torn garment for a dead person, nor make permanent inscriptions on your bodies. For I am the Lord your God.
You must not defile your daughter so that she becomes a prostitute and the land becomes filled with lawlessness.
You must keep my Sabbaths and revere my holy places. I am the Lord your God.
You must not follow idols or those who summon the dead, nor approach those who invoke spirits, so that you become defiled by them. I am the Lord your God.
You shall rise and stand before a gray-haired person, honor an elder, and fear the Lord your God. I am the Lord your God.
If a foreigner comes to live among you in your land, you shall not oppress him.
The foreigner who comes to live among you shall be like a native among you. You shall love him as yourself, because you too were foreigners in the land of Egypt. I am the Lord your God.
You shall not act unjustly in judgment, in measures, in weights, or in scales.
You shall have honest scales, honest weights, and an honest liquid measure. I am the Lord your God, who brought you out of the land of Egypt.
You shall keep my entire law and all my commands and carry them out, because I am the Lord your God.
And the Lord spoke to Moses, saying:

Speak to the Israelites, saying: If anyone among the Israelites, or among the foreigners who have joined Israel, gives any of his offspring to a ruler, he must be put to death. The people of the land shall stone him with stones.

I myself will set my face against that man and destroy him, cutting him off from his people, because he gave some of his offspring to a ruler, defiling my holy places and profaning the name of those whom I have purified for myself.
But if the inhabitants of the land deliberately turn a blind eye to that man when he gives his offspring to the ruler, and do not put him to death,
I will set my face against him and his family. I will destroy him and everyone who joins him in prostituting themselves with the rulers, cutting them off from their people.
If a person turns to mediums or those who summon spirits, prostituting themselves by following them, I will set my face against that person and destroy them, cutting them off from their people.
You shall be holy, because I, the Lord your God, am holy.
You shall keep my ordinances and carry them out, because I am the Lord who makes you holy.
If a man insults his father or his mother, he must be put to death. Whoever speaks evil against his father or his mother shall be liable to death.

If a man commits adultery with another man's wife, or whoever commits adultery with his neighbor's wife, he must be put to death. The adulterer and the woman with whom adultery was committed shall suffer the same death.
And anyone who sleeps with his father’s wife has uncovered his father’s nakedness. They must both be put to death; both of them are guilty.
Whoever sleeps with his daughter-in-law must be put to death. Both of them deserve it.
Whoever sleeps with a male as one sleeps with a woman has committed an abomination. Both of them shall be put to death together. They deserve death.
Whoever takes a woman and her mother commits lawlessness. He shall be burned with them in a fire, so that there may be no lawlessness among you.
Whoever sleeps with an animal must be put to death, and you shall also kill the animal.
If a woman approaches any animal to have it mate with her, you shall kill the woman and the animal. They must be put to death. They deserve death.

Whoever takes his sister, his father's daughter or his mother's daughter, and sees her nakedness commits a disgrace. Both of them shall be cut off before the children of their people, because he has exposed his sister's nakedness. He shall bear his sin.

If a man sleeps with a woman during her menstrual period and exposes her nakedness, he has exposed the source of her blood, and she too has exposed the blood flowing from her. Both of them shall be cut off from their people.
You shall not expose the nakedness of your father's sister or your mother's sister, for he has exposed his own relative. They shall bear their sin; they shall die childless.
Whoever sleeps with his female relative has exposed the nakedness of his own relative. They shall die childless.
Whoever takes his brother's wife commits an unclean act. He has exposed his brother's nakedness. They shall die childless.
You shall keep all my ordinances and my judgments and carry them out, so that the land into which I am bringing you to live will not hate you.
And you must not follow the customs of the nations that I will drive out before you, because they did all these things, and I detested them.
And I told you, ‘You will inherit their land, and I will give it to you as an inheritance, a land flowing with milk and honey.’ I am the Lord your God, who separated you from all the nations.

You must distinguish between clean and unclean animals, and between clean and unclean birds. You must not make yourselves detestable through animals, birds, or any of the creeping creatures of the earth that I have set apart for you as unclean.
You must be holy to me, because I, the Lord your God, am holy. I am the one who separated you from all the nations so that you would be my people.
And if a man or a woman is a medium or calls up spirits, they must be put to death. You must stone them with stones. They deserve death.
And the Lord said to Moses, ‘Speak to the priests, Aaron’s sons, and tell them: They must not defile themselves through dead persons among their people,
except for a close relative: a father or mother, sons or daughters, a brother or a sister of his.
For the virgin who is closely related to him, who has not been given in marriage, he may defile himself. He may do so for these relatives.
He must not suddenly defile himself among his people, bringing defilement upon himself.
And you must not shave your heads for a corpse. They must not shave the hair of their beards, and they must not cut their flesh.

Instead, they must be holy to their God and must not defile the name of their God, because they are the ones who will offer up the Lord’s sacrifices, the gifts of their God. Therefore they must be holy.
He must not marry a prostitute or a woman who has been defiled. He must not marry a woman whose husband has divorced her, because he is holy to the Lord his God.
And you must sanctify him. He is the one who will offer up the gifts of the Lord your God. He must be holy to me. I am the Lord; I am holy, the one who sanctifies them.
And if the daughter of a priest defiles herself by engaging in prostitution and defiles her father’s name, she is the one who defiles him. She must be burned with fire.

And the priest who is greatest among his brothers, on whose head the anointing oil has been poured and whose hands have been purified so that he may put on the holy garments, must not uncover his head or tear his clothes.
And he must not go in to any person who has died. He must not defile himself for his father or his mother.
And he must not leave the holy place or defile what has been sanctified and belongs to his God, because the holy anointing oil of his God is upon him. I am the Lord.
He must marry a virgin woman from his own family.
But he must not marry a widow, a divorced woman, a defiled woman, or a prostitute. Instead, he must marry a virgin woman from his own family.
He must not defile his offspring among his people. I am the Lord who sanctifies him.
And the Lord spoke to Moses, saying:
Say to Aaron: A man from your family, throughout your generations, who has a bodily defect must not approach to offer up the gift of his God.
No man who has a bodily defect may approach: a man who is lame or blind, whose nose is shortened, or whose ear is torn,
or a man with a broken hand or a broken foot,
or who is hunchbacked or [?], or has a cataract in his eyes, or a man with severe scabies or a skin eruption, or who has only one testicle—that is, a single testicle.
No one among the descendants of Aaron the priest who has a physical defect may approach to offer a sacrifice to his God, because he has a defect. He must not approach to present the gifts of his God.
The gifts of God are the most holy things, and he may eat from all the holy things.
But he must not go inside the curtain or approach the altar, because he has a defect. He must not defile God's sanctuary, for I am holy; I am the Lord who makes them holy.
And Moses spoke to Aaron, his sons, and all the Israelites.
And the Lord spoke to Moses, saying:
Tell Aaron and his sons to keep themselves away from the Israelites' sacred offerings, so that they do not defile my holy name through the things they dedicate to me. I am the Lord.

Tell them: Any person among all your descendants, throughout your generations, who approaches the sacred offerings that the Israelites dedicate to the Lord while he is unclean—that person will be cut off from my presence. I am the Lord.

And any descendant of Aaron the priest who has leprosy or a discharge must not eat any of the sacred offerings until he is cleansed. The same applies to anyone who touches any uncleanness from a dead body, or a man who has an unclean discharge of semen,
or anyone who touches an unclean crawling creature that makes him unclean, or touches a person and becomes unclean through any kind of uncleanness that person has.
The person who touches such a thing will be unclean until evening. He must not eat any of the sacred offerings unless he washes his body with water.
When the sun has set, he will be clean, and he may eat the sacred offerings, because they are his food.
He must not eat an animal that has died or one that a wild animal has killed. I am the Lord.
They must keep my requirements, so that they do not incur sin because of these things and die for defiling them. I am the Lord who makes them holy.
No outsider of foreign ancestry may eat the sacred offerings. A guest staying with the priest or a hired worker must not eat the sacred offerings.
But if the priest acquires a person by purchasing him with money, that person may eat his food. Those born in his household may also eat his food.
If a priest's daughter marries an outsider, she must not eat any of the firstfruits of the sacred offerings.

And if a priest’s daughter becomes a widow or is divorced and has no offspring, she shall return to her father’s house as in her youth and eat her father’s bread. But no outsider of foreign birth may eat it.
And anyone who unknowingly eats any of the holy things shall add a fifth of its value to it and give the holy thing to the priest.
They must not defile the Israelites' sacred offerings, which they offer to the Lord,
nor bring guilt for sin upon them by eating their sacred offerings, for I am the Lord who makes them holy.
And the Lord spoke to Moses, saying:

Speak to Aaron, his sons, and the whole assembly of the Israelites, and tell them: Any individual among the Israelites who brings his offering in fulfillment of their vows or as any of their voluntary offerings, which they bring to offer to the Lord as a burnt offering—
what you bring must be choice and without defect, from your cattle, your sheep, or your goats.
They must not bring anything with a defect to offer to the Lord, because it will not be accepted on your behalf.

And anyone who brings a peace offering to offer to the Lord, having made a voluntary vow, or at your festivals, must bring a choice animal from the cattle or sheep, without defect. It must have no defect at all.

An animal that is blind, broken, has its tongue cut, has a wart, has a severe scab, or has a skin eruption—you must not bring these to offer to the Lord. You must not offer any of them as a burnt offering on the altar as a fire offering to the Lord.
A calf or sheep whose ears are cut off or whose tail is cut off may be slaughtered and kept for you to eat, but you must not bring it to fulfill your vow.

An animal with crushed testicles—that is, one that has been crushed—or one with testicles that have been bruised, torn out, or cut off, you must not bring to offer to the Lord. You must not produce such animals in your land.
And you must not accept any of these from a foreigner to bring as your offerings, offering them as a fire offering to your God, because they are damaged. They will not be accepted on your behalf.
And the Lord spoke to Moses, saying:
When a calf, a sheep, or a goat is born, it shall remain with its mother for seven days. From the eighth day onward, it may be taken and offered as a burnt offering to the Lord.
You must not slaughter a cow or a sheep together with its young on the same day.
If you slaughter a sacrifice in fulfillment of a vow to the Lord, you shall slaughter it so that it will be accepted on your behalf.
You must not eat it on that day, and you must not leave any of its meat until morning. I am the Lord.
You shall keep my commandments and carry them out, for I am the Lord,
And you must not profane the name of the Holy One. I will be held holy among the Israelites, for I am the Lord who makes you holy.
who brought you out of the land of Egypt to be your God. I am the Lord.
And the Lord spoke to Moses, saying to him,
“Speak to the people of Israel and tell them: These are the Lord’s festivals whose names you shall proclaim as holy festival days. These are my festivals.

For six days you shall do your work, but the seventh day is a Sabbath. You shall call that day the Lord’s holy rest. You must not do any work on it. It is a Sabbath to the Lord in all your dwelling places.
These are the Lord’s festivals, and these are the holy days whose names you shall proclaim at their appointed times.
In the first month, on the [?] day of the month, in the evening, is the Lord’s Passover.
And on the eighteenth day of this same month is the Lord’s Festival of Unleavened Bread. You shall observe it for seven days, [?] unleavened bread.
And the first day shall be proclaimed holy for you. You must not do any ordinary work on it.
And you shall bring your burnt offerings and present them to the Lord for seven days. The seventh day shall be proclaimed holy for you. You must not do any ordinary work on it.
And the Lord spoke to Moses, saying:
“Speak to the people of Israel and tell them: When you enter the land that I am going to give you and reap your harvest, you shall bring a sheaf of the firstfruits of your harvest to the priest.
He shall lift up the sheaf before the Lord so that it will be accepted on your behalf. On the day after the first day, the priest shall lift it up.
On the day when you bring the sheaf, you shall offer a year-old sheep without blemish as a burnt offering to the Lord.
Its grain offering shall be two tenths of fine flour mixed with oil, an offering to the Lord with a pleasing aroma before the Lord. Its drink offering shall be wine, a quarter of a hin.

You must not eat bread or crushed new grain until that very day, until you yourselves bring your gifts before God. This shall be a permanent statute for you throughout your generations, in all your dwelling places.
You shall count for yourselves seven complete weeks from the day after the Sabbath, from the day when you bring the sheaf to lift it up.
You shall count them until the day after the last day. You shall count four final days, and you shall bring a new offering [?] to the Lord.
From your dwelling places you shall bring bread to lift up: two loaves made from two tenths of fine flour. They shall be purified and baked as firstfruits to lift up to the Lord.

With the bread you shall bring seven lambs without blemish that are about a year old, a young calf, and two rams without blemish that are about a year old. They shall be a burnt offering to the Lord, and their grain offerings and drink offerings shall be an offering with a pleasing aroma to the Lord.
And you shall offer one male goat from the goats as a sin offering, and two lambs a year old as a peace offering, together with the bread of the first produce.

The priest shall lift them up before the Lord with the bread from the first crop that he harvested and with the two lambs. They shall be holy to the Lord. They shall belong to the priest who lifts them up.
And you shall proclaim that day holy for you. You must not do any work on it. It is not fitting for it to be a perpetual statute for you in all your settlements throughout your generations.

When you reap the harvest of your land, [?] the harvest of your field, you must not gather it completely, and you must not gather what falls during your harvest. You shall leave it for the poor and the foreign resident, for I am the Lord your God.
And the Lord spoke to Moses, saying:
“Speak to the people of Israel and tell them: In the seventh month, on the first day of the month, you shall have a rest, a celebration with trumpets, and that day shall be holy for you.
You must not do any work on it. It is not permitted for you to bring your burnt offerings to offer them to the Lord.
And the Lord spoke to Moses, saying:
On the tenth day of the seventh month, there is a day of prayer for forgiveness. It shall be holy for you, and you shall humble yourselves and bring your burnt offerings to the Lord.
You must not do any work on it, for it is a day of atonement for you, to make atonement for you before the Lord your God.
Anyone who does not humble themselves on that day shall be cut off from their people.
And anyone who does any work on that day shall be put to death and removed from their people.
You must not do any work. This shall be a permanent rule for you throughout your generations, in all your dwelling places.
It shall be a Sabbath of complete rest for you, and you shall humble yourselves. Beginning on the ninth day of the month, from evening to evening, you shall observe your Sabbaths.
And the Lord spoke to Moses, saying:
Speak to the Israelites and tell them: On the fifteenth day of this seventh month is the Festival of Shelters. The festival shall last seven days for the Lord.
And the first day shall be proclaimed holy. You must not do any work that is improper.
For seven days you shall bring your burnt offerings to the Lord. It is a closing festival. You must not do any work on it; that is not permitted.

These are the Lord's festivals, which you shall proclaim as holy, so that you may present your offerings to the Lord: burnt offerings and their sacrifices, offered to the Lord, and daily drink offerings, day by day.
These are in addition to the Lord's Sabbaths, your ordinances, all your vows, and all your voluntary offerings that you shall give to the Lord.

And on the fifteenth day of the seventh month, when you have finished gathering the produce of your land, you shall celebrate a festival for the Lord for seven days. The first day is a day of rest, and the seventh day is a day of rest.

And on the first day you shall take fruit from beautiful trees, and [?], or palm branches, and branches of trees with abundant leaves, and a chaste tree—that is, a willow—from a stream or flowing water. You shall rejoice before the Lord your God and celebrate the Lord’s festival for seven days each year.
This is a permanent rule throughout your generations: you shall celebrate this festival in the seventh month.
You must not live in shelters for seven days. Every native-born person in Israel shall live in shelters.
When I brought them out of the land of Egypt. I am the Lord your God.
And Moses proclaimed the Lord's words to the Israelites.
And the Lord spoke to Moses.
Command the Israelites to bring you oil of [?], that is, pure, pressed olive oil, to put in the lamp and light it so that it gives light at all times.
Outside the curtain of the testimony, Aaron and his sons shall keep it burning from evening until morning before the Lord continually. This is a permanent rule throughout your generations.
He shall light the lamp on the holy lampstand before the Lord until morning.
And you shall take fine flour and make it into twelve loaves. Each loaf shall contain two-tenths of a measure of flour.
And you shall arrange them in two rows. In the first row, you shall set down six loaves on the holy table before the Lord.
And you shall put pure frankincense and salt on them, so that they become pure loaves for remembrance, placed before the Lord.
From the Israelites at all times, as an everlasting covenant.

They shall belong to Aaron and his sons, who shall eat them in a holy place, for they are most holy. This shall be their portion from the offerings made as sacrifices to the Lord, as a permanent rule.
And the son of an Israelite woman, whose father was an Egyptian, went out among the Israelites. The son of the Israelite woman and an Israelite man fought in the camp.
And the son of the Israelite woman pronounced [?] the Name and cursed. They brought him before Moses. His mother's name was Shelomith, the child of Dibri, from the tribe of Dan.
And they put him in custody so that his case could be decided through the Lord's command.
The Lord spoke to Moses, saying:
“Bring the man who cursed outside the camp. Those who heard him must lay their hands on his head, and the whole congregation must stone him.
And you must speak to the Israelites, saying to them, ‘If anyone curses God, he will bear the guilt of his sin.
But whoever utters the name of the Lord must be put to death with stones. The whole congregation must stone him. Whether he is a convert or a native, when he utters the name of the Lord, he must die.
And if anyone strikes any human being and that person dies, he must be put to death.
And whoever strikes an animal and it dies must give a life for a life.
And if anyone injures his neighbor, what he did to his neighbor must likewise be done to him:
a fracture for a fracture, an eye for an eye, a tooth for a tooth. According to the injury he inflicts on another person, you must repay him for these things.
And whoever strikes a person and that person dies must certainly die.’
There shall be one law for the foreign resident and the native, for I am the Lord your God.
And Moses spoke to the Israelites, saying to them, “Bring the man who cursed outside the camp, and let them stone him.” And the Israelites did as the Lord had commanded Moses.
And the Lord spoke to Moses on Mount Sinai, saying:
“Speak to the Israelites, saying to them, ‘When you enter the land that I am going to give you, you must give rest to the land that I am going to give you, observing the Lord’s Sabbaths.
You must sow your field for six years, and you must prune your grapevine for six years and gather its fruit.
But the seventh year is a Sabbath, when the land must rest and you must observe the Lord’s Sabbaths. You must not sow your field or prune your grapevine.
And you must not reap what grows by itself in your field, or gather the grapes you have set apart. It must be a year of rest for your land.
They will be yours to eat, along with your male slave, your female slave, your hired worker, the foreigner staying with you, and anyone attached to your household,
as well as your livestock and the wild animals in your land. All its produce will be theirs to eat.
And you must count seven periods of rest for yourself, seven years seven times, making seven periods of seven years for you, that is, forty-nine years.
And you must announce it with the sound of a trumpet throughout your land in the seventh month. On the day of the prayer for forgiveness, you must sound a trumpet throughout your land.

You must consecrate the fiftieth year and proclaim release throughout the land to everyone living in it, because it is a year of release. This will be a sign for you, and each person must return to the property he owns, and each of you must return to your family.
This is the sign of release in the fiftieth year, which will be such a year for you. You must not sow, or reap what grows by itself in it, or gather what has been consecrated in it.
For it is a sign of release for you, and it must be holy. You must eat the produce of the field.
In the year of release, at its signal, each person must return to his property.
If you sell something to your neighbor, do not let anyone cheat his neighbor.
You must buy from your neighbor according to the number of years after the signal. He must sell to you according to the number of years of harvests.

As the years increase, he must increase the price he receives for his property; as the years decrease, he must reduce the price of his property, because he is selling to you according to the number of harvests.
Do not let anyone oppress his neighbor, and you must fear your God, for I am the Lord your God.
You must carry out all my ordinances and keep all my judgments and obey them, so that you may live securely in the land.
The land will bring forth its crops, and you will eat them until you are satisfied and live securely on it.
But if you say, “What will you eat in this seventh year, when we do not sow and you do not gather your crops?”
I will send you my blessing in the sixth year, and it will yield its produce for three years.
You will sow in the eighth year and eat the old stored provisions. You will eat from the produce until the ninth year, until its produce comes in, [?] old provisions.
The land must not be sold into permanent ownership, for the land is mine, because you are immigrants and foreign residents before me.
Throughout all the land of your inheritance, you must allow the land to be redeemed.
But if your brother who lives with you becomes poor and sells part of his inheritance, and his nearest relative wishes to redeem his brother’s inheritance, he shall redeem it.
But if he has no close relative, and he acquires the means and finds the man [?] for his redemption,
He must calculate the years since its sale, pay what he owes to the man to whom he sold it, and return to his inheritance.

But if he cannot find enough to repay him, the property he sold will belong to the person who bought it until the year of release. It will be released at the release, and he will return to his inheritance.
If someone sells his dwelling house in a city with a wall built around it, it may be redeemed until a full year of days has passed. For eight years it may be redeemed.

But if it is not redeemed before its full year has ended, the house in the city with a wall built around it will belong permanently—that is, securely—to the person who bought it and to his descendants. It will not be released at the release.
But the houses in villages with no wall built around them will be counted as fields of the land. They may be redeemed at any time, and they will be released at the release.
And the cities of the Levites, the houses in the cities of their inheritance, may be redeemed at any time, and they will belong to the Levites.

And if someone redeems property from the Levites, the [?] of the houses in the city of their inheritance will be released at the time of release, because the houses in the cities of the Levites are their allotted portion among the children of Israel.
And the other fields set apart for their cities must not be sold, because this allotted portion is their inheritance forever.
If your brother becomes poor and has no means of support beside you, you must help him as you would an immigrant or a foreign resident, so that your brother may live with you.
You must not take interest from him or charge him extra. You shall fear your God, for I am the Lord, so that your brother may live with you.
You must not lend him your money at interest, and you must not give him your food for a profit.
I am the Lord your God, who brought you out of the land of Egypt to give you the land of Canaan and to be your God.
If your brother becomes poor beside you and is sold to you, he must not serve you as slaves serve.
Instead, he will be with you like a hired worker or like a foreign resident. He will work for you until the year of release.
At the time of release, he will leave your service, he and his children with him. He will return to his family and go back to the land of his father's inheritance.
For they are my slaves, whom I brought out of the land of Egypt. They must not be sold as a slave is sold.
You must not oppress him harshly with suffering, but you must fear your God.
Your male and female slaves whom you acquire will come from the nations around you. From them you may acquire a male slave and a female slave.
You may also acquire slaves from the children of the foreign residents living among you and from their relatives who will be in your land. They will belong to you as your property.

You will pass them on to your children after you, and they will remain under your authority, so that you may rule over them forever. But as for your brothers, the Israelites, none of you must oppress his brother with harsh treatment.

If a foreign resident or an alien living near you becomes prosperous, while your brother becomes poor and destitute and is sold to the foreign resident or the alien living near you, or to a foreign resident born in his household,
after he has been sold, he may be redeemed. One of his brothers shall redeem him.
His father's brother or the son of his father's brother shall redeem him, or a blood relative from his tribe shall redeem him. If he has the means, he may redeem himself.

He shall calculate with the person who bought him the years from when he sold himself to him until the year of his release. The money paid for him shall be reckoned according to the yearly rate of a hired worker; he shall remain with him at that yearly rate.
If many years remain, he shall pay his redemption price in proportion to them, out of the money paid for him.
If only a few years remain until the year of release, he shall reckon with him according to those years and pay him his redemption price.
He shall remain with him like a hired worker, year by year. You must not oppress him with harsh treatment before your eyes.
If he is not redeemed in these ways, he shall go free in the year of release, together with his children.
For the Israelites are my slaves. They are my slaves whom I brought out of the land of Egypt. I am the Lord your God.
You must not make handmade idols for yourselves, or [?], or set up a pillar for yourselves, or place a stone for worship in your land to bow down to it. I am the Lord your God.
Keep my Sabbaths and revere my holy places. I am the Lord.
If you walk according to my commands and keep my commandments and carry them out,
I will give you rain in its season. I will give it so that the land produces its crops, and the trees of the fields will bear their fruit.
Your threshing will last until your grape harvest, and the grape harvest will last until sowing time. You will eat your bread to the full and live securely on your land.
I will give peace to your land, and you will sleep restfully, with no one to frighten you. I will destroy the dangerous wild animals in your land, and no war will come upon your land.
You shall pursue your enemies, and they shall fall before you in fear.
Ten of you shall pursue a hundred men, and a hundred of you shall pursue ten thousand men. Your enemies shall fall before you by the sword.
I will look upon you and make you numerous, and I will establish my covenant with you.
You will eat old stored grain, and [?] the old grain before the new.
I will establish my covenant among you, and my soul will not reject you.
I will walk among you and be your God, and you yourselves will be my people.
I am the Lord your God, who brought you out of the land of Egypt, where you were slaves. I broke the bond of your yoke and brought you out boldly.
But if you do not listen to me and do not carry out these commands of mine,
but instead disobey them, and your soul hates my judgments, so that you do not carry out all my commandments and thus break my covenant,

I, in turn, will do these things to you: I will bring deprivation, skin disease, and jaundice upon you. It will strike your eyes, and deprivation will destroy your lives. You will sow your seed in vain, and your enemies will eat it.
I will set my face firmly against you, and you will fall before your enemies, and those who hate you will pursue you.
If, even after these things, you do not listen to me, I will go on disciplining you with seven plagues for your sins.
And I will break your arrogant pride. I will make the sky above you bronze, and I will make your land iron.
Your strength will be spent in vain. The land will not give you its produce, and the trees of the field will not give you their fruit.
And if, after these things, you continue to act perversely and refuse to listen to me, I will add seven plagues upon you for your sins.
And I will send the wild beasts of the land among you. They will devour you and consume your livestock. They will reduce your numbers, and your roads will become deserted.
If these things do not discipline you, but you still act perversely against me,
I too will deal with you in anger and perversity, and I too will strike you seven times for your sins.

And I will bring a sword upon you to exact vengeance from you under the judgment of my covenant. You will flee into your cities, and I will send death among you. You will be handed over to all your enemies so that they may oppress you.
When a shortage of bread afflicts you, ten women will bake your bread in a single oven. They will give you your bread by measure, and you will eat without being satisfied.
But if, despite these things, you do not listen to me, but act perversely against me,
I too will deal with you perversely, in anger, and I will discipline you seven times for your sins.
You will eat the flesh of your sons; you will also eat the flesh of your sons.
I will make your pillars desolate, and I will destroy the wooden objects fashioned by your hands. I will lay the remains of your bodies upon the remains of your idols, and my soul will hate you.
And I will leave your cities desolate. I will burn your holy places, and I will not smell the fragrance of your sacrifices.
I will make your land desolate, and you will be astonished. Your enemies who live in it will also be astonished at it.
And I will scatter you among the nations, and the sword shall come against you and destroy you, and your cities shall lie deserted.
Then the land will observe its Sabbaths throughout all the days when it lies desolate, while you yourselves are in the land of your enemies. The land will observe its Sabbaths
and remain in them throughout all the days of its desolation. It will take the rest that it did not take during the Sabbaths in the times when you lived there.

And as for those who remain among you, I will send [?] terror down into their land, in the land of their enemies. The sound of a moving leaf will chase them, and they will flee like someone fleeing from war. They will fall when no one is pursuing them.
One brother will fall upon another as in war, though no one is pursuing them. You will not have the strength to fight your enemies.
You will perish among the nations, and the land of your enemies will devour you.
And those who remain among you will perish because of their sins and waste away in the land of their enemies.
And they will confess their sins and the sins of their ancestors: that they transgressed, abandoned me, and acted perversely before me.
I too dealt with them in anger and perversity, and I will destroy them in the land of their enemies. Then their uncircumcised heart will be ashamed, and they will recognize their sins.
Then I will remember the covenant with Jacob, and the covenant with Isaac, and the covenant with Abraham. I will remember it, and I will also remember the land.

And I will leave the land behind them. After these things, the land will receive its Sabbaths as it becomes desolate because of them. They too will pay for their lawlessness, because they abandoned my judgments and hated my commandments in their souls.
And even when they were in the land of their enemies, I did not neglect them or hate them so as to destroy them and break my covenant established with them, because I am the Lord their God.
And I will remember their former covenant, when I brought them out of the land of Egypt, out of the house of their slavery, before the nations, to be their God. I am the Lord.
These are the rulings, regulations, and law that the Lord established between himself and the Israelites on Mount Sinai through Moses.
And the Lord spoke to Moses, saying:
Speak to the Israelites and tell them: If someone makes a vow to give the value of his own person to the Lord,
the valuation for the Lord, from twenty years old up to sixty years old, shall be fifty silver staters according to the sanctuary measure.
But the valuation of a woman shall be thirty staters.
If the age is from five years to twenty, the valuation of a male shall be twenty staters, and the valuation of a female shall be ten staters.
From one month old to five years old, the valuation of a male shall be five silver staters, and the valuation of a female shall be three silver staters.
If the age is sixty years or more, the valuation of a male shall be fifteen silver staters, and that of a female shall be ten staters.
But if he is poor or lacks the amount of his valuation, he shall stand before the priest, and the priest shall assess his value.
If it is one of the animals from which offerings are presented to the Lord, whatever someone gives to the Lord from these shall be holy.

You must not substitute another in its place, a good one for a bad one or a bad one for a good one. If someone does exchange one animal for another, both the animal itself and its replacement shall be holy.
If it is any unclean animal, one of those from which offerings are not presented to the Lord, he shall bring the animal before the priest.
And the priest shall assess its value; he shall set its price on that basis.
But if someone redeems it, he shall add one-fifth to its valuation.
If someone consecrates his house to be holy to the Lord, the priest shall assess its value, considering its good and bad qualities. Whatever value the priest assigns to it shall stand.
But if the person who consecrated his house redeems it, he shall add one-fifth of the silver amount of its valuation, and it shall belong to him.
Every firstborn among your animals shall belong to the Lord, and no one shall consecrate it. Whether it is a calf or a sheep, it shall belong to the Lord.

But if it is one of the unclean animals, he shall redeem it according to its valuation and add one-fifth to it, and it shall belong to him. If he does not redeem it, it shall be sold for the amount of its valuation.

But anything that someone devotes to the Lord by a vow from everything he owns—whether a person, an animal, or a field of his inheritance—he must neither sell nor redeem. Everything devoted shall be most holy to the Lord.
And anything that people dedicate shall not be redeemed; it must be put to death.
Every tithe of the land, whether from the seed of the land or from the fruit of a tree, belongs to the Lord and shall be holy to the Lord.
If someone redeems his tithe, he shall add one-fifth to it, and it shall belong to him.
Every tithe of the cattle and sheep, and of everything that passes under the staff to be counted—the tenth shall be holy to the Lord.
You must not exchange a good one for a bad one. But if you do exchange it, both it and its replacement shall be holy; it shall not be redeemed.
These are the commandments that the Lord entrusted to Moses on Mount Sinai to proclaim to the Israelites.
